page: Microsoft Azure D16pds_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the DPDSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The system is configured with 64.0 GB of memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance includes a 614 GB SSD and supports Premium Storage. There are no GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses bundled with this server.

Benchmark data places the D16pds_v5 in the average tier for most multi-core and memory operations. It achieves a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 28887.7 and a PassMark CPU score of 11617.1. Memory bandwidth is measured at 1125.92 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 129.87 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. However, single-core performance is a notable tradeoff, with Geekbench single-core scores of 1108.0 and single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 8.83 GB/sec falling into the weak performance category. Cryptographic performance is also limited, as indicated by a weak PassMark CPU encryption score of 2591.19, which correlates with the lack of advanced vector and matrix extensions.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture provides a resource-dense profile with a balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio and integrated local SSD storage, offering a qualitative advantage for workloads that scale horizontally across multiple physical cores. The instance is suited for general-purpose workloads, static web serving with 17.95 GB/sec throughput, database operations with 11285.91 PassMark database operations, and multi-threaded software compilation. It is less suited for single-threaded tasks, heavy cryptographic processing, or large-scale LLM inference.
